Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the packet you sent last week. Two quick follow-ups from our architecture team as we map Redwood into our controlled-inference zone: 1) can you provide a matrix that enumerates expected runtime interactions between the inference enclave (model runtime), sidecar proxies, control plane, and any storage or telemetry endpoints? We aim to validate Greenline's supply-chain acceptance criteria next Thursday; a concise narrative plus a diagram would be perfect. If possible, include any fallback behaviour (e.g., model variant fallbacks / canary rollback) and how routing preserves tenant separation.

Appreciate it — Samir

Samir —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached are two artifacts: a compact interaction matrix (PNG) and a short egress/control summary (PDF). Below is a quick narrative; the attachments have the detailed mapping you requested.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- We treat the model runtime (inference enclave) as a sealed execution domain. The only permitted inbound flows are authenticated request tokens (mutually TLS) from the data plane front-door. All persistent storage (checkpoints, KV cache dumps) is encrypted at rest and stored in tenant-scoped object stores when enabled — by default we keep KV only in memory.
- Sidecar proxies provide TLS termination and request validation; they run in a distinct process boundary and only forward metadata needed for routing (no plaintext user content persist).
- Control plane interactions are strictly outbound-only from the runtime to the control plane (telemetry / health) over a mutually authenticated channel; customer-configured VPC peering or PrivateLink is supported.
- Fallbacks: automatic model variant fallback and canary rollback are enforced by routing policies at the routing layer; a failing variant is isolated to a circuit and traffic re-routed to a compatible variant with identical tenant isolation.

Key attack-surface notes (high level):
- Lateral movement: we assume an adversary that can compromise a single compute instance but not the control plane HSM/KMS or customer network fabric. Isolation relies on kernel and container process boundaries + mandatory sidecar filters.
- Data-in-transit: mTLS for all internal RPCs; TLS 1.3 preferred ciphers; intra-zone traffic is authenticated with short-lived certs issued by the control plane CA.
- KV cache persistence: default = in-memory only. If a customer opts into persistence for warm-starts, the cache is encrypted with tenant keys and stored in a per-tenant bucket; access logged and audited.

Attached artifacts: redwood_runtime_enclave_matrix_v2.png (interaction matrix + legend), egress-control-summary.pdf (controls, fallback choreography, and audit evidence pointers).

Happy to jump on a quick technical call with your team to walk the diagram.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Samir / Vivek — quick clarifying note after reviewing the matrix:
- Sidecar-to-runtime: only a minimal set of headers are proxied (request-id, tenancy-id, and routing-hash). We intentionally strip any client-supplied authorization headers before they reach the runtime and re-inject short-lived session creds issued by the sidecar when needed.
- Egress categorization: we mark telemetry (prom/trace) as "low-sensitivity egress" but health-heartbeat metadata as "sensitive" because it includes instance provenance. Both channels are over mTLS with record-level audit.

If Greenline requires an air-gapped option (we note many healthcare customers ask), we can provide a Private control plane deployment pattern; we'll enumerate the additional attestation artifacts if you confirm that's the route.

-Priya

Samir — Vivek / Priya, adding a short operational runbook note here for Greenline's auditors:
- Canary & rollback: when a model variant is promoted, traffic is mirrored to the canary pool with 1–5% traffic. Health and quality guards (latency, failure rate, quality regressions) are evaluated; if thresholds breach, the routing layer triggers a rollback and marks the variant as quarantined. That circuit-level quarantine preserves tenant separation — no traffic is routed to the quarantined instances.
- Incident evidence: we can provide time-series traces and token-level cost/latency slices for any timeframe (retention configurable). For regulated evidence requests we produce a packaged export with signed timestamps.

If Greenline is ready, I'll book a 45-minute technical walk-through (Priya and I will join) — propose Wed 2026-11-03 10:00 PST / 13:00 EST. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include the Drive folder with the artifacts and a short pre-read.
